A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dynamic Token Morphing (DTM) research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and formatting changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original pilot experiments, ImageNet classification and ADE20K segmentation results, transfer-learning evaluations, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including those moved into appendices, and adds an 800-epoch pre-training result.

M1.justification: The dynamic scheduling, bipartite matching, shared morphing matrix, weighted cosine loss, and accumulation across morphing cases remain unchanged. Revised descriptions and Figure 3 clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K/100, ADE20K, the same three iNaturalist datasets, and Birds, CUB-200, CIFAR-10/100, and Dogs. Transfer evaluations move from v2 Section 5.4 to v3 Appendix B without changing coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 adds MaskSub and LUT as reported comparators. The separate baseline-versus-DTM backbone comparison in v2 Table 5 disappears; its CLIP-based ViT-S/L baseline entries are not retained elsewhere. Other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 Section 5.1 adds an 800-epoch pre-training experiment alongside the retained 300-epoch evaluations. Existing fine-tuning protocols, transfer-learning grid searches, and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged after matching relocated material.

E4.justification: v3 adds a longer-training observation but removes v2's dedicated backbone-scalability analysis and Table 5. The loss, morphing-step, scheduling, randomness, normalization, and dynamic-mechanism ablations remain, including those relocated to the appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions report best accuracy and mean ± standard deviation across transfer-learning hyperparameter searches. Relocating those tables introduces no change in uncertainty reporting, and no new seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v3 adds 85.5% ImageNet accuracy after 800 pre-training epochs. Table 3 adds MaskSub/LUT results and an ExtreMa ViT-S score of 81.8, and revises ViT-S scores for iBOT from 82.3 to 82.0 and ConMIM from 79.8 to 82.0. The removed scalability table loses baseline scores of 82.7/86.4 for ViT-S/L. DTM's 300-epoch scores of 83.2/85.4/86.7 and ADE20K result of 53.1 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), morphing-matrix constraints, sampling distributions, and objective definitions are mathematically unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3's abstract explicitly claims faster training and reduced losses, making acceleration more definite than v2's introductory conjecture. The central DTM, spatial-inconsistency, applicability, and transferability claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 Section 5.1 interprets the new 800-epoch result as evidence that longer pre-training helps and claims an advantage over methods trained for 1600 epochs, including BEiT v2. It also predicts further gains from longer training. Existing mechanism explanations and the limitation concerning models larger than ViT-L remain.

D1.justification: Most training details are preserved through consolidation into v3 Appendix E. However, v2's explicit statement that all models were pre-trained on eight V100-32GB GPUs is omitted; the separate ADE20K fine-tuning hardware disclosure remains. Hyperparameter tables and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for MaskSub, LUT, and the Birds, Dogs, and CIFAR datasets. The related-work discussion retains its positioning of DTM as using token aggregation to improve supervision rather than primarily compress tokens.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative: pilot-study subsections are merged, experimental discussions are reordered, transfer learning and selected ablations move into appendices, and training descriptions are consolidated. The abstract, introduction, method explanations, and appendix overview also receive extensive editing.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different template and page layout. Figures 1 and A are redrawn with image-patch overlays and revised bounding-box displays; Figure 3 explicitly depicts individual losses and their sum. Multiple tables are relocated and reformatted, and the standalone scalability table is removed.

improvement.justification: The revised loss diagram and broader comparator coverage add value, while most original evidence is preserved. However, v3 removes the matched ViT-S/L baseline evidence and pre-training hardware disclosure. Its new claim of outperforming 1600-epoch BEiT v2 lacks a corresponding numerical comparison in the supplied PDFs. These explanatory gains and reporting losses leave the net quality change uncertain.
